chunks: With this chain, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

One who recites Surah al-Talaq and Surah al-Tahrim in his obligatory prayer, Allah will protect him from being among those who fear or grieve on the Day of Judgment, and he will be saved from the Fire, and Allah will admit him into Paradise due to his recitation of them and his perseverance upon them, because they are for the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.سُورَةَ التَّحْرِيمِ: Surah al-Tahrim (The Prohibition), the 66th chapter of the Quran
key_terms.سُورَةَ الطَّلَاقِ: Surah al-Talaq (The Divorce), the 65th chapter of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Talaq and Tahrim in obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq links the recitation of Surah al-Talaq and Surah al-Tahrim to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), emphasizing their unique spiritual efficacy in obligatory prayers. This practice is believed to secure protection from fear and grief on the Day of Judgment, deliverance from Hellfire, and entry into Paradise, reflecting the Shia tradition of connecting specific Surahs to the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. From the previous chain from al-Hassan b. Ali from al-Hussain b. Abi al-’Ala from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “

One who recites Surah Talaq and Tahrim in his obligatory prayers the Almighty Allah would protect him from the fear of the Day of Judgment and save him from Hell. He would enter Paradise due to recitation of these Surahs for they are related to the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.).”
